fact: The National Bank of Ethiopia licenses ETTA's ZooryaPay as a Payment System Operator, per the Capital newspaper report.

Directive 1069/2025 defines payment service providers as those licensed or authorized by the National Bank of Ethiopia to issue payment instruments, and requires federal public bodies to accept payments from all of them.

ITWeb Africa reports Ethiopia has joined PAPSS, with NBE governor Eyob Tekalign saying the move deepens continental ties, enabling financial institutions in the country to connect for instant cross-border payments.
The National Bank of Ethiopia and PAPSS announced on 15 October 2026 that Ethiopia has officially joined the PAPSS network, letting Ethiopian financial institutions connect for cross-border payments.

Digital Policy Alert states that the National Bank of Ethiopia has exclusive authority to license payment system operators and issuers of payment instruments, and issued a licensing and authorisation directive in October 2023.
Connecting Africa reports that Safaricom Ethiopia was given a Payment Instrument Issuer licence by the National Bank of Ethiopia, three months before M-Pesa went live in August 2023.

Onafriq's release says Safaricom M-PESA Mobile Financial Services received a Payment Instrument Issuer License from the National Bank of Ethiopia in May 2023 and went operational in August 2023, and that the Bank authorised its remittance service in July 2023.
The Reporter says Kacha Digital Financial Service is Ethiopia's first privately owned payment instrument issuer licensed by the National Bank of Ethiopia.
